caption:
The Union carries a rich legacy from its origins as the Pomona YMCA, first opened in 1922. Designed by architect Robert Hall Orr in a Georgian Revival style, the three-story, 50,000-square-foot structure began construction in 1920, with its cornerstone laid in June of that year—a ceremony rooted in the YMCA’s tradition of symbolizing both foundation and future. Such events often drew national attention; even Theodore Roosevelt once spoke at a YMCA cornerstone laying in Vallejo. The Pomona YMCA’s dedication followed on April 18, 1922, with California Governor William Stephens addressing the community.

Artifacts and symbols throughout the building reflect the YMCA’s global heritage. The Chi-Rho, one of the earliest symbols of Christ used in the Roman catacombs, connects the local branch to the deep history of Christian faith. The YMCA triangle—representing the holistic development of mind, body, and spirit—remains a reminder of its mission. Inscribed in many YMCA spaces is John 17:21, calling for unity: “That they all may be one.” This echoes the spirit of the Paris Basis of 1885, drafted under the leadership of YMCA founder Sir George Williams, which declared that differences should never disrupt the harmony of the worldwide movement.

Originally begun in England, the YMCA became a unifying force for communities around the world, and Pomona’s building stands as a living artifact of that vision—where faith, fellowship, and civic life intertwined to shape a cornerstone institution of the city.

caption:
The Union at Garey (Pomona YMCA) is a winner for the 2025 Preservation Design Award for Rehabilitation from the California Preservation Foundation.

"The Pomona YMCA had fallen from being a symbol of pride and gathering place of the Pomona community to a deteriorating building that the YMCA could no longer afford to maintain and dormitory housing that the community wanted closed.

The project scope was to provide public benefit for the community. Assembly areas were adapted into a community event center with state-of-the-art lighting, sound, LED wall and commercial kitchen. Stores, professional services and cafe line the lobby that serves as a community gathering space.

The basement locker and exercise rooms were adapted into the owner’s company headquarters and the upper residential floors into offices.

Reviving this National Register building was possible only through an owner willing to accept lower rentable area by restoring open areas and lower rents to include community-serving non-profits. The project is a model that shows the success of preservation is measured more than just by dollars."

Read more about The Union at Garey rehabiliation project: https://californiapreservation.org/awards/pomona-ymca/

caption:
Being principal for a day at the high school I once attended was a surreal experience. As I stood in front of a whole new generation of students, I felt both humbled and inspired.

The opportunity allowed me to witness firsthand how much has evolved over the years. It was a privilege to interact with the principal Dr. Green students, teachers, and staff, seeing the dedication that makes this place so special. I felt a deep sense of connection to the legacy of my school, with my old teachers knowing that the impact I once experienced as a student is now being passed on to those who walk through these doors.

This experience was a reminder of the profound influence education has on shaping us. The teachers who mentored me, the friends who supported me, and the lessons learned within these walls have all played an integral role in the person I am today. To be able to give back, even for just one day, is something I will cherish forever.

Thank you to the amazing faculty and staff who welcomed me with open arms. Here’s to the future of this school, and PUSD.

✅ DONATION DROP OFF
Alliance Community Cultural Center
406 W. 2nd St, Pomona, CA 91766
10am-7pm 1/9-1/11
@pomona4as 

Items Needed:
FOOD & WATER : Bottled water, non-perishable food, baby formula
CLOTHING & BLANKETS : New socks, underwear, warm clothing, blankets, sleeping bags (MUST BE NEW)
HYGIENE : Toothpaste, soap, diapers, feminine hygiene products, hand sanitizer
MEDICAL : First aid kits, over-the-counter medications, bandages
EVACUATION SUPPORT : Flashlights, batteries, phone chargers, pet food
GIFT CARDS : Groceries, gas, or major retailers

*They are coordinating thier donation efforts with Pasadena Senior Center and other local entities.

✅ EVACUATION SHELTER
Pomona Fairplex 
601 W. McKinley Ave, Pomona, CA 91768
Enter through Gate 3
*Red Cross Emergency Shelter

Red Cross is providing food, water, medical services and mental health services are available at the shelter.

✅ AirBNB SUPPORT
211LA.org

AirBNB is partnering with 211LA to provide tree temporary housing for people who have been displaced by the LA wildfires.
